key_insight: A small set of attention heads can causally influence whether a multimodal AI follows images or text when they disagree. These “arbitration heads” offer a targeted way to control how the model resolves conflicting evidence.
problem_solved: Multimodal models can favor one modality even when it is less reliable for the task, making their answers unreliable when visual and textual inputs conflict.
method: Study model predictions when visual and textual evidence disagree.
Identify attention heads that causally influence whether predictions follow visual or textual evidence.
Use these arbitration heads as a basis for lightweight inference-time control; the supplied abstract is truncated before the full method is described.
impact: This work points toward more controllable multimodal systems that need not rely on a fixed preference for images or text. Practitioners could potentially steer conflict resolution at inference time, although the supplied excerpt does not establish performance gains.

paper_title: Beyond Modality Preference: Controlling Multimodal Arbitration under Modality Conflict in MLLMs
paper_authors: Zhaoying Pan, Shenyu Lu, Jun Hui Wong, Junyi Chai, Xiaoqian Wang
